chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'Can anyone escape from the squeezing of the grave?' He said, 'We seek Refuge with Allah from it. How few are the ones who would escape from the squeezing of the grave.'

Indeed, when Uthman killed Ruqayya, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) stood by her grave, raised his head to the sky, his eyes shed tears, and he said to the people: 'I remembered this one and what she had faced, so I melted for her and gifted her escape from the squeezing of the grave.'
He said: 'O Allah! Endow to me, Ruqayya being free from the squeezing of the grave.' So Allah gifted it to her, for him.

He said: 'And indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) went out in the funeral of Sa'd, and seventy thousand angels had escorted him. So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) raised his head to the sky, then said: 'The likes of Sa'd would be squeezed.'
I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you! We are narrating that he used to belittle with the urine (uncleanness).' So he said, 'Allah Forbid! But rather, he was with harsh mannerisms upon his family.'
He said: 'So the mother of Sa'd said, 'Congratulations to you, O Sa'd!' So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to her: 'O mother of Sa'd! Do not impose it upon Allah!'
ai.seo_question: Who escapes the squeezing of the grave according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi highlights the Shia belief in the physical squeezing of the grave (Dagh-t al-Qabr) while emphasizing that exemption is a specific divine mercy rather than a universal right. It illustrates this through the Prophet’s prayer for Ruqayya’s exemption and the contrasting fate of Sa’d, whose seventy thousand angels of escort did not spare him from the squeeze despite his virtue and minor character flaws (Za’arrah). The narrative underscores the theological principle that even the righteous are subject to the grave's trial unless Allah grants them specific reprieve.

en.sarwar: 6. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from ‘Uthman ibn ‘Isa from Ali ibn abu Hamzah from abu Basir who has said the following:

“I asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ‘Can anyone remain safe from the pressure of the grave?’ The Imam said, ‘I seek protection against it from Allah. How few are those who remain safe from the pressure in the grave!

When Ruqiyyah was murdered..., the Messenger of Allah stood on her grave and raised his head toward the sky, his eyes flooded with tears, and said to people, “I thought of her and her condition in the grave moved me to a weeping state. I pleaded before Allah to give her safety from the pressure of the grave as a gift for me.’”
He (the Imam) has said that the Messenger of Allah then said, “O Lord, save Ruqiyyah from the pressure of the grave as gift to me.” Allah then granted him that gift.

The Messenger of Allah took part in the funeral of Sa‘d in which seventy thousand angels had also taken part. The Messenger of Allah raised his head to the sky and said, ‘Even (a person like) Sa‘d undergoes the pressure of the grave.’

I then said to the Imam, ‘It is said that he (Sa‘d) would not pay much attention to the uncleanness from his urine.’ He replied, ‘May Allah grant protection, it was due to his harsh manners toward his family (wife).’

The Imam then said that mother of Sa‘d said, ‘How fortunate are you, O Sa‘d!’ the Messenger of Allah then said, ‘O mother of Sa‘d, please do not consider it (granting an opportune) an obligation upon Allah.’”
